Everyone talks about ainetworking, but most investors completely misunderstand the two distinct battlegrounds: Scale-Out vs. Scale-Up. Scale-Out: Connecting racks to other racks across a data center. This is a long-distance game and already relies heavily on optical fiber. Scale-Up: The backend fabric connecting GPUs directly to GPUs so they act as one giant, logical brain. Today, this is almost entirely copper (like NVIDIA's NVLink). The problem? As aifactories scale to massive clusters of 10,000 to 1,000,000 GPUs, the physical distance between chips grows. Copper is fast and cheap, but it hits a physical wall at short distances due to severe signal degradation and thermodynamic limits. You simply cannot bridge massive, multi-rack gpuclusters with copper cables. The inevitable solution is that optics must invade the Scale-Up domain. To bridge these distances without melting power budgets, the industry is transitioning to Co-Packaged Optics (CPO). This shift from copper to light in the backend gpunetwork unlocks a massive, entirely greenfield $9 billion tamby 2030.$NVDA : Set to transition its proprietary NVLink to optical CPO (Feynman architecture) to scale GPU-to-gpuconnections across data centers.$MRVL&$AVGO: Marvell acquired Celestial aito place optical interconnects directly on XPUs to break the memory wall, while Broadcom is leading the charge in open-ecosystem cposilicon and switches.$LITE&$COHR: Copper doesn’t need lasers, but cpodoes.
